entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Abd-al-Razzāq Samarqandī was a Persian Timurid chronicler and Islamic scholar. He was for a while the ambassador of Shah Rukh, the Timurid dynasty ruler of Persia. In his role as ambassador he visited Kozhikode in south India in the early 1440s. He wrote a narrative of what he saw in Calicut which is valuable as information on Calicut's society and culture. He is also the producer of a lengthy narrative or chronicle of the history of the Timurid dynasty and its predecessors in Central Asia, but this is not so valuable because it is mostly a compilation of material from earlier written sources that are mostly available from elsewhere in the earlier form.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Abd-al-Razzāq Samarqandī's account of Calicut provides valuable insights into the society and culture of South India during the early 15th century, with his visit to Kozhikode in 1440 marking one of the earliest recorded European-Asian interactions. His chronicle of the Timurid dynasty also sheds light on the historical context of Central Asia during this period.
